page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an arm64 architecture powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU configuration provides one thread per core, avoiding hyperthreading overhead, and includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The D32ps_v6 achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 450.97 GB/sec and write speeds of 188.48 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Multi-core processing is a notable strength, as evidenced by strong ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core tests, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations also perform in the top tier, registering 37356.46 on Passmark. However, single-core performance remains average, and large-model LLM inference prompt processing is poor, registering at 4.64 tokens per second.

From a resource density perspective, the ARM-based architecture offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for deployments relying on external network storage. This server is suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
